about: Austin Ginder's Wavelength recreations of the game's synth sound recipes, picked by Austin on 2026-11-01 (tools/sound/wavelength-sfx/takes.json). Each file plays for the keys listed with it, in place of its js/synth-sfx.js recipe; keys with a recovered Tiny Speck recording keep the recording (recordingKeys).
author: Austin Ginder

licence.own-work: CC0 1.0: rendered by Austin Ginder from his own Wavelength job, procedural sources only
licence.own-work+MIT: CC0 1.0 for Austin Ginder's arrangement and render; the MuseScore General samples heard in it stay under MIT, notice in MuseScore_General_License.md beside the files

method: Wavelength job (tools/sound/wavelength-sfx/jobs/<recipe>.json) rendered at 48 kHz, trimmed and levelled by the WAVESFX lane, delivered as 44.1 kHz stereo 160 kbps MP3; installed by tools/sound/install-wavelength-sfx.mjs as mono 96kbps CBR MP3 peaked at -1 dBFS. gainDb = short-sound LUFS of the synth recipe's render minus the shipped file's.

rounds.about: Clean-licence round: round one's notes, timing and levels re-rendered on MuseScore General and Wavelength's builtin:synth (clean.py).
Redo round: three candidates each for burp, sneeze and fireworks (redo.py); burp is still open.

Round one: the first Wavelength take of each recipe (make-jobs.py, render-all.py). Austin approved the 16 whose sources were clean already; the rest of his round-one picks shipped from the clean round or are held here for their samples.

coin.how: MuseScore General Glockenspiel B6 to E7, the classic coin.
coin.author: Austin Ginder

chime.how: MuseScore General Celesta E5 B5 E6 doubled softly by its Vibraphone.
chime.author: Austin Ginder

craftDone.how: A MuseScore General Glockenspiel A6 ping, then Celesta G5 B5 D6.
craftDone.author: Austin Ginder

magic.how: A MuseScore General Harp glissando A4 to A5 over a faint violin slide, with the sparkle (Celesta, Glockenspiel above C7, synth air) on top.
magic.author: Austin Ginder

sneeze.how: All breath: two whispered "ah" intakes, then a sharp "ch" hiss and a noise "oo" falling from 2.5 kHz: ah-ah-choo.
sneeze.author: Austin Ginder

fireworks.how: A thin sine whistle with a tail of rising air, a timpani boom with a low noise thump, then dense crackle and glockenspiel sparks.
fireworks.author: Austin Ginder

mapClose.how: Three falling paper flicks folding shut on a faint low woodblock tap.
mapClose.author: Austin Ginder

cardFlip.how: Two crisp filtered-noise flicks, the second lower, with a faint stick tap: a card flipping.
cardFlip.author: Austin Ginder

gong.how: An additive gong on C3 (inharmonic partials blooming) over a soft timpani stroke and a tubular bell.
gong.author: Austin Ginder

hoeScrape.how: One long guiro stroke: the hoe scraping soil.
hoeScrape.author: Austin Ginder

sizzle.how: High hissing noise with cabasa crackles popping through it: a frying pan.
sizzle.author: Austin Ginder

shake.how: Six alternating maraca and shaker hits: a cocktail shaker.
shake.author: Austin Ginder

hiss.how: High-passed noise opening upward with a breath on top: gas escaping.
hiss.author: Austin Ginder

squishSoft.how: A soft squelch: resonant low-passed noise closing down over a sine sagging from D4.
squishSoft.author: Austin Ginder

flutter.how: Fluttering wing noise (a tremolo on filtered noise) and a short bird tweet.
flutter.author: Austin Ginder

mew.how: A violin sliding F5 up to C6 and sagging back: a kitten mew.
mew.author: Austin Ginder

ribbit.how: Two short guiro strokes (the wooden frog) over a low bassoon blip: ribbit.
ribbit.author: Austin Ginder

sloth.how: A slow, sleepy bassoon E3 sagging to A2 with a lazy vibrato.
sloth.author: Austin Ginder

rustle.how: Five leafy noise rustles with a cabasa and a shaker brush.
rustle.author: Austin Ginder

croak.how: A bassoon and cello groaning from G#4 down nearly three octaves, landing on a timpani and a sub drop.
croak.author: Austin Ginder

squish.how: A juicy squelch: resonant noise closing from 1.8 kHz to 260 Hz over a sine falling from C4.
squish.author: Austin Ginder

whoosh.how: A band-passed air whoosh sweeping 400 Hz to 2.6 kHz with a breath.
whoosh.author: Austin Ginder
